description:
A schematic map illustrating typical land cover / land use (LCLU) morphology in an estuarine environment, using simplified polygons for four distinct classes. The legend defines the colour coding:
*   Grey (8.3.2): Estuaries, representing the main body of the river where it meets the sea.
*   Light pink (7.2.1): Salt marshes, flanking the estuarine channels and tidal areas.
*   Blue (8.4.0): Sea and ocean, depicting the open water body into which the estuary flows.
*   Olive green (6.1): Sparsely vegetated areas, located further inland or along the higher banks of the estuary, bordering the salt marshes.
The map shows a branching pattern of estuaries (grey) flowing into the wider sea and ocean (blue), with extensive areas of salt marshes (pink) distributed along the estuarine banks and within tidal flats. Sparsely vegetated areas (olive green) are depicted further inland, adjacent to the upper reaches of the estuarine arms. This configuration illustrates the typical transition of land cover types from terrestrial to marine environments within an estuary.
